verdict.rationale: Visa Intelligent Commerce is API-first. Its core lifecycle is documented as REST endpoints: card enrollment (POST /acp/v1/tokens), purchase-intent mandates and cancellation (POST /acp/v1/instructions), and credential retrieval. The same APIs are also exposed through an official MCP server. However, no evidence states API/UI parity, and onboarding runs through a web sign-up form and the Test Enterprise Business Center, with no documented API equivalent. Missing for 10: an explicit API/UI parity statement, API coverage of onboarding and Business Center functions, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: Your agents can enroll a customer's card for tokenization during the customer's account registration or when the customer begins a new purchase intent
Your agent can cancel a purchase intent when the customer chooses to not make the purchase.
Developers can now connect to Visa Intelligent Commerce APIs through the MCP Server
